page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is an entry-tier instance in the compute-optimized C2D family, powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors built on x86_64 architecture. Hardware specifications include 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyperthreading enabled, 8.0 GB of RAM, 32 MB of L3 cache, and no local storage or attached GPUs. Network configuration provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core execution, with stress-ng single-threaded CPU throughput reaching the top 25 percent of tested systems. Single-threaded gzip compression and small-model LLM text generation also show solid average performance. Conversely, multi-core tests, memory bandwidth metrics, and Redis database operations fall into lower benchmark categories due to the physical constraint of having only one physical core and modest memory allocations.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the c2d-standard-2 provides a low-overhead entry point for applications requiring dedicated AMD EPYC clock cycles without paying for unneeded memory or storage density. Primary workload fits include lightweight static web serving, single-threaded processing scripts, basic CI/CD execution, and internal development servers.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is a virtual server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs from 1 physical core, 2.0 threads per core, and 8.0 GB of memory, equating to 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes 32 MB of L3 cache but contains no local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs. In performance benchmarks, the c2d-standard-2 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests and average results for single-threaded compression and text generation. However, multi-core processing scores, memory bandwidth, and database transaction rates fall in lower performance percentiles due to hardware resource constraints. This server configuration offers a cost-efficient entry point within the compute-optimized family, making it suitable for lightweight web applications, basic utility tasks, and developer environments requiring stable single-thread core execution.
